name: mp++
workload: Vectors of 3e7 small (1-2 limb) integers: dot product, multiply-add, truncated division, sort, shifts, gcd/lcm
claimed_speedup: dot product almost 4x faster than GMP; vector multiply-add more than 7x; vector division about 8x (1-limb unsigned)
tradeoffs: Built on GMP/MPFR/MPC; gains come from small-buffer optimisation, so large operands see no gain.
caveats: Benchmark page gives no CPU, compiler or flags; gains narrow for signed integers; first-party numbers.
found_via: WebSearch: multiprecision integer arithmetic library faster than GMP benchmark C++ github

name: CTBignum
workload: Fixed-width (2-4 limb) multiprecision arithmetic and modular operations, runtime and compile-time, for cryptography
claimed_speedup: outperforms GMP for small operands (2-4 limbs); GMP wins at 8+ limbs (no ratios extracted)
compiler_and_flags: Apple LLVM 9.0.0, -O3, some benchmarks -march=native, no LTO
hardware: 2017 MacBook Pro, quad-core 2.3 GHz Intel Core i5 (Kaby Lake), Turbo Boost disabled
tradeoffs: C++20 header-only, fixed-size, constexpr-capable; not all functions constant-time.
caveats: Only small operand sizes; GMP is faster at 8+ limbs; 2018 hardware and compiler; speedup numbers not quoted from the paper tables.
found_via: WebSearch result Multiprecision Arithmetic for Cryptology in C++ (arXiv 1804.07236)

name: FLINT
workload: 100 million digits of pi; 100x100 integer matrix multiplication at 10/100/1000-bit entries
claimed_speedup: pi: GMP 62.1 s vs FLINT 31.6 s single-thread (about 2x) and 9.34 s on 8 threads (6.6x, derived from page data); 100x100 matmul 10-bit entries 0.0122 s vs 0.00395 s naive, optimised 8-thread 0.0000675 s
tradeoffs: Uses GMP/MPIR underneath; FLINT 3 absorbs Arb, Calcium; fft_small is AVX2/NEON tuned.
caveats: First-party; compiler/flags not given; FLINT naive matmul is not faster than GMP at 100/1000 bits; github issue 2852 reports fft_small slower than GMP on a Zen 5 EPYC (not opened).
found_via: WebSearch: FLINT fmpz arithmetic faster than GMP benchmark

name: Arb (dot product and matrix multiplication)
workload: Arbitrary-precision dot product (p=53..848 bits) and 1000x1000 matrix multiplication at p=3392
claimed_speedup: up to 3.7x faster than MPFR for floating-point dot product, ball dot product up to 2.0x faster than MPFR at low precision; cycles/term at p=53: 40 (Arb ball) vs 169 (MPFR); p=212: 133 vs 277; p=848: 522 vs 705
tradeoffs: Interval (ball) arithmetic with error bounds, different semantics from MPFR rounding; merged into FLINT.
caveats: Repo archived, development moved to FLINT (already listed above); compiler flags not stated; basic Arb multiplication is only about 1.0x MPFR (Arb paper 1611.02831 Table 2).
found_via: WebSearch: Arb ball arithmetic faster than MPFR benchmark

name: Truncated batch SIMD AVX512 Montgomery multiplication
workload: Batch Montgomery multiplication and fixed-window modular exponentiation, 260-4154 bit operands using AVX512 VPMADD52
claimed_speedup: Montgomery multiplication 5.34x (1024-bit) to 3.95x (4096-bit) vs GMP; fixed-window exponentiation 5.42x to 4.66x vs GMP; vs OpenSSL 3.69-4.31x
hardware: Dell Inspiron laptop, 11th Gen Intel Core i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz, Turbo Boost disabled
tradeoffs: Needs AVX512-IFMA; batch (SIMD across independent operands) not single-operation latency.
caveats: Batch throughput compared with per-operation GMP; results are for modular arithmetic, not general bigint; last commit not checked; benchmark code assumed public in repo (README not read in full).
found_via: WebSearch: arXiv big integer multiplication outperforms GMP AVX-512 IFMA

name: DigitsOnTurbo (DoT)
workload: Large-number addition, subtraction, multiplication with x86 SIMD intrinsics, plus pi computation
claimed_speedup: addition/subtraction up to 3.81x geometric mean; multiplication up to 1.41x geometric mean; pi computation up to 19.3%; multiplication of larger operands up to 48.7%
hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 6548Y+ (Emerald Rapids) and Xeon Max 9462 (Sapphire Rapids)
tradeoffs: 1,013 lines of portable C with intrinsics; integrates into GMP and OpenSSL with ~40 lines of changes.
caveats: Code only at an anonymous review URL (anonymous.4open.science/r/DigitsOnTurbo, not opened); no license found; preprint not peer-reviewed; geometric-mean figures are for best cases.
found_via: WebSearch: arXiv big integer multiplication outperforms GMP AVX-512 IFMA

name: midint-arithmetic-division (GPU multi-precision division)
workload: Batched shifted-inverse integer division on GPU for 2^13 to 2^18-bit operands
claimed_speedup: 11.3x faster than GMP at 2^18 bits; 14.0x at 2^17; 18.9x at 2^16; 12.6x at 2^15; 7.4x at 2^14; 11.1x at 2^13
tradeoffs: Requires NVIDIA GPU; batched workloads; CUDA/Futhark.
caveats: Repo is a fork of coancea/midint-arithmetic (parent URL not opened); license not found; GPU vs CPU GMP comparison; README says it does not beat CGBN in its range; uses CUDA so not a plain C++ library.
found_via: WebSearch: GPU CUDA multiple precision integer arithmetic library faster than GMP
